transcript.content: Hi, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. What brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you too, Dr. Smith. Well, what made me come in is that for the past year or so, the smallest thing just pulls me off what I’m doing before I can even stop it. It could be a phone buzz, somebody walking past my office, or... I don't know, even a random thought about my in-laws. It just completely takes my attention away from my work.
Did you notice similar problems with being easily distracted back when you were a child or teenager, or is this something that's really only started in the past year?

Well, looking back... no, it's not just a recent thing. It was definitely around when I was a kid, too. I remember teachers were pretty much always moving my seat around the classroom. I guess I just talked way too much, or I'd get up out of my desk without asking first. And I had a bad habit of just... blurting things out before they even finished asking the question. So yeah, it's been there for a long time.
Do you still notice yourself feeling restless, needing to move around, or acting impulsively—like interrupting others or making quick decisions without thinking—now as an adult?

Yeah, I definitely still get restless. If I'm supposed to just sit still... like during family dinners or at church volunteer meetings, it honestly feels like there's a motor running inside me. I just get this urge where I need to move around, or at least find something to do with my hands.
Would you say these difficulties with distractibility and restlessness have caused real problems for you—like at work, in your relationships, or in other areas of daily life?

Well, I'm still keeping up overall, for the most part. But... yeah, it is starting to cause some real issues. It’s starting to cost me trust at home, mostly when family plans just don't go the way they should. And at work... I can tell people are losing their patience with me. Especially when meetings or, you know, mentoring conversations with my staff don't go how they're supposed to because I get sidetracked or can't just sit and listen. So it hasn't completely ruined anything, but it's definitely causing a lot of friction.
Do you still find yourself frequently interrupting or finishing other people's sentences, or making decisions quickly without thinking them through, in your daily life now?

Yeah, I do. I've been cutting people off more lately. Like, if my wife is talking to her parents, I'll just jump right into the middle of their conversation. Or at work, I'll end up finishing an employee's thought before they're even done talking. I don't mean to do it, but I just... do it. And I can definitely tell it rubs people the wrong way.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a lifelong (since childhood) pattern of inattention (easy distractibility by minor stimuli, difficulty maintaining focus in work/meetings), hyperactivity (inner restlessness, need to move, fidgeting), and impulsivity (interrupting, blurting answers, finishing others' sentences). Symptoms were present before age 12 (classroom seat changes, talking excessively, blurting) and persist into adulthood, causing functional impairment in occupational (work meetings, mentoring) and relational (family trust, spousal interactions) domains. The combination of significant inattentive and hyperactive-impulsive symptoms meets criteria for combined presentation, ICD-10 F90.2 (Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, combined type).
